translation_en: Abu Thalabah al-Khushani said, I asked the Prophet, We live among People of the Book and in a land where game is plentiful. May we eat from their vessels? I hunt with my bow, with an untrained dog, and with my trained dog; what is lawful for me? He said, As for their vessels, if you find others, do not eat from theirs. If you cannot find others, wash them and then eat from them. Whatever you hunt with your bow, after mentioning Allah's name, you may eat. Whatever your trained dog catches after you mention Allah's name, you may eat. If your untrained dog catches game and you reach it while it is still alive, slaughter it and eat it.

Abdullah bin Mughaffal saw a man using a small pebble to shoot and told him not to do so, for the Messenger of Allah forbade it or disliked it. The Prophet said it neither catches game nor harms an enemy, but it may break a tooth or put out an eye. Later he saw the man doing it again and said, I tell you the Messenger of Allah forbade or disliked this, yet you still do it. I will not speak to you for such-and-such a time.

Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet said, Whoever keeps a dog, except a dog for herding livestock or hunting, loses two qirats from his deeds every day. The report is from Musa bin Ismail, from Abd al-Aziz bin Muslim, from Abdullah bin Dinar, who heard Ibn Umar relate it from the Prophet.

Ibn Umar said he heard the Prophet say that whoever keeps a dog, except one trained to hunt or guard livestock, loses two qirats from his reward each day. Salim said he heard Abdullah bin Umar, who said he heard the Prophet give this instruction.

Ibn Umar reported that the Messenger of Allah said, Whoever keeps a dog, except a dog for livestock or hunting, loses two qirats from his deeds each day. Nafi narrated this wording from Abdullah bin Umar.

Adi bin Hatim said, I asked the Messenger of Allah about hunting with trained dogs. He said, When you send your trained dogs after mentioning Allah's name, eat what they catch for you, even if they kill it, unless the dog eats from it. I fear then that it caught the prey for itself. If other dogs join yours, do not eat it.

Adi bin Hatim reported that the Prophet said, If you send your dog after naming Allah, and it catches and kills the prey, eat it. If it eats from it, do not eat, because it caught it for itself. If dogs over which Allah's name was not mentioned join it, and they catch and kill prey, do not eat, because you do not know which dog killed it. If you shoot game and find it after a day or two with no mark other than your arrow's, eat it; but if it falls into water, do not eat it.
Adi said he asked the Prophet about game he shot and tracked for two or three days, then found dead with his arrow in it. The Prophet said, Eat it if you wish.

Adi bin Hatim said, Messenger of Allah, I send my dog after naming Allah. The Prophet said, If you send your dog after naming Allah, and it catches, kills, and eats the prey, do not eat it, because it caught it for itself. Adi said he might find another dog with his own and not know which caught the prey. The Prophet said not to eat it, because he had mentioned Allah's name over his own dog, not the other. Adi also asked about hunting with a mihraz. The Prophet said to eat what it strikes with its sharp edge, but not what it kills with its broad side, for that is a beaten animal.

Adi bin Hatim said, We hunt with these dogs. The Prophet said, When you release your trained dogs after mentioning Allah's name, eat what they catch for you, even if they kill it, unless they eat it. If they eat, do not eat it. If other dogs join them, do not eat it. The narrators are Muhammad, Ibn Fudayl, Bayan, Amir, and Adi bin Hatim.

Abu Thalabah al-Khushani asked about living among People of the Book, using their vessels, and hunting with a bow and trained or untrained dogs. The Prophet said not to eat from their vessels if other vessels were available; otherwise wash them first. He instructed him to mention Allah's name when hunting with a bow or trained dog and then eat the catch. If an untrained dog caught game and he reached it while it was still alive, he could slaughter and eat it. Abu Thalabah said he lived among People of the Book and asked about their utensils and hunting. The Prophet told him to avoid their dishes when other dishes were available; if not, wash them first. He instructed him to invoke Allah's name when using the bow or a trained dog, then eat the catch. With an untrained dog, if he found the animal alive, he was to slaughter it before eating.

Anas said they startled a rabbit at Marr al-Zahran. The people ran after it until they were tired. Anas pursued it and caught it. He brought it to Abu Talhah, who sent its haunch and thighs to the Prophet, and the Prophet accepted them.

Abu Qatadah said he was with the Messenger of Allah on part of the road to Mecca. He fell behind with some Companions who were in ihram, while he was not. He saw a wild donkey, mounted his horse, and asked his companions to hand him a whip. They refused, and they also refused his spear. He took it himself, charged the donkey, and killed it. Some of the Prophet's Companions ate from it and some refused. When they caught up with the Messenger, they asked him about it. He said, It is food Allah has provided for you.

Abu Qatadah reported the same account, except that the Prophet asked, Do you have any of its meat with you? This version is transmitted by Malik, from Zayd bin Aslam, from Ata bin Yasar, from Abu Qatadah.

Abu Qatadah said he was with the Prophet between Mecca and Medina. The others were in ihram, while he was not. He was a skilled rider among the hills and saw people looking toward something. He went to see and found it was a wild donkey. They said they did not know what it was, and he identified it. He had forgotten his whip and asked them to pass it to him, but they would not help. He went down, took it, pursued the donkey, and brought it down. He carried it back to them, but some refused to touch it and others ate. He went to the Prophet and told him what happened. The Prophet asked if any remained. Abu Qatadah said yes, and he replied, Eat; it is food Allah has provided for you. Abu Qatadah was riding a horse while in a state permitting him to hunt. He pursued and killed the donkey, carried it back to the others, and some ate while others did not. He brought the question to the Prophet, who asked whether any meat remained and permitted them to eat it as food Allah had provided.

Jabir said they went on the Army of al-Khabt, commanded by Abu Ubaidah. They became extremely hungry. The sea cast up a huge dead whale called al-Anbar, unlike anything they had seen. They ate from it for half a month. Abu Ubaidah took one of its bones and a rider passed underneath it.

Jabir said the Prophet sent three hundred riders under Abu Ubaidah to watch a Quraysh caravan. They suffered severe hunger and ate leaves, so the expedition was called the Army of al-Khabt. The sea cast up a whale called al-Anbar, and they ate it for half a month and used its fat. Their bodies recovered. Abu Ubaidah set up one of its ribs, and a rider passed underneath it. One man, when the hunger grew severe, slaughtered three camels, then three more, until Abu Ubaidah stopped him.

Ibn Abi Awfa said they went on six or seven military expeditions with the Prophet and ate locusts with him. Sufyan, Abu Awanah, and Israil reported the number as seven. Ibn Abi Awfa said they ate locusts on military expeditions with the Prophet, whether the count was six or seven. The named transmitters report seven.

Abu Thalabah al-Khushani asked the Prophet about living among People of the Book, eating from their vessels, and hunting with a bow and with trained or untrained dogs. The Prophet said not to eat from their vessels unless there was no alternative; if necessary, wash them and eat. He said to mention Allah's name and eat what was hunted with a bow or trained dog. If an untrained dog caught prey and the hunter reached it while it was still alive, he should slaughter it and eat it. Abu Thalabah al-Khushani asked about the dishes of the People of the Book and hunting equipment. He was told to wash their dishes if no alternative was available. For game hunted with a bow or a trained dog, he should mention Allah's name and eat. If an untrained dog caught the animal and he reached it while it was alive, he should slaughter it first.

Salamah bin al-Akwa said that when evening came on the day they conquered Khaybar, people lit fires. The Prophet asked what they were cooking. They said domestic donkey meat. He ordered them to pour out what was in the pots and break the pots. A man asked if they could pour out the meat and wash the pots instead. The Prophet said, Or do that.

Rafi bin Khadij said they were with the Prophet at Dhul-Hulayfah when hunger struck and they obtained camels and sheep. The Prophet was at the rear while people hurried and set up cooking pots. When the Prophet arrived, he ordered the pots overturned. He then distributed the animals, assigning ten sheep for each camel. One camel ran off. The group had only a few horses and could not catch it. A man shot it with an arrow and stopped it. The Prophet said, These animals can bolt like wild animals; if one escapes you, deal with it this way. Rafi said his grandfather asked whether they could slaughter with reeds when they feared meeting the enemy the next day and had no knives. The Prophet said, Whatever makes the blood flow and has Allah's name mentioned over it, eat, except teeth and nails. I will explain: a tooth is a bone, and a nail is the knife of the Abyssinians.

Abdullah reported that before revelation came to the Messenger of Allah, he met Zayd bin Amr bin Nufail at the lower part of Baldah. The Messenger offered him meat from a meal spread out, but Zayd refused to eat. He said, I do not eat what you slaughter at your stone altars; I eat only what Allah's name has been mentioned over. Abdullah related that the Messenger met Zayd before revelation had come. Zayd refused the offered meal because it included meat sacrificed at stone altars. He said he would eat only meat over which Allah's name had been mentioned.

Jundab bin Sufyan al-Bajali said they offered a sacrifice with the Messenger of Allah one day. Some people had slaughtered their sacrifices before the prayer. When the Prophet finished praying and saw this, he said, Whoever slaughtered before the prayer must slaughter another in its place. Whoever had not slaughtered until after we prayed should slaughter in Allah's name.

A shepherd girl of theirs tended sheep at Sal. She saw one sheep dying, broke a sharp piece from a stone, and slaughtered it. Her owner told his family not to eat until he asked the Prophet or sent someone to ask. He went or sent a messenger, and the Prophet ordered them to eat it. The report says the shepherd girl broke a sharp stone and slaughtered a sheep that seemed to be dying. Her owner waited for the Prophet's ruling, and the Prophet allowed the household to eat it.

A girl belonging to Kab bin Malik grazed his sheep at a small hill by the market at Sal. When a sheep was injured, she broke a stone and slaughtered it. They mentioned it to the Prophet, and he ordered them to eat it.

Abayah bin Rafi said his grandfather told the Messenger of Allah, We have no knives. He said, Whatever makes the blood flow and has Allah's name mentioned over it, eat, except teeth and nails. A nail is the knife of the Abyssinians, and a tooth is a bone. A camel escaped, and the people stopped it. The Prophet said these camels can bolt like wild animals, so deal with one that escapes in this way.

A woman slaughtered a sheep with a stone. The Prophet was asked about it and ordered that it be eaten. Al-Layth reported from Nafi that he heard an Ansari man tell Abdullah this same report about a girl belonging to Kab. The report came through Nafi, from Ibn of Kab bin Malik, from his father. Al-Layth also related the account from Nafi through an Ansari man.

A girl belonging to Kab bin Malik grazed his sheep at Sal. One sheep was injured; she reached it and slaughtered it with a stone. The Prophet was asked about it and said, Eat it. The narrator was uncertain whether the Ansari was Muadh bin Sad or Sad bin Muadh.
Rafi bin Khadij reported that the Prophet said, Eat what makes the blood flow, except a tooth or a nail. Rafi bin Khadij reported this concise ruling from the Prophet about slaughtering an animal.

Aishah said some people told the Prophet that meat was brought to them by people and they did not know whether Allah's name had been mentioned over it. He said, Mention Allah's name over it yourselves and eat it. Aishah said those people had only recently left disbelief. Ali reported the same from al-Darawardi, as did Abu Khalid and al-Tufawi.
